findings.issue: The 14 Sep 1914 front already stood on the Dunajec–Biała line (identical to the 26 Sep key), so the Austro-Hungarian retreat jumped ~12 days early and Przemyśl showed as Russian before its siege began (16 Sep). 14 Sep now runs along the San (Austrian retreat ordered 9–11 Sep, 'general withdrawal behind the San'); 26 Sep keeps the Dunajec–Biała line confirmed by USMA map 29 (line of 28 Sep). The Russian Galicia ring's 14 Sep key follows the new line.

Between Lemberg (3 Sep) and the retreat the map slid straight from the 31 Aug line to the retreat line, hiding the Rawa Ruska/Gródek stand (3–11 Sep). Added a 9 Sep front (Gródek–Rawa Ruska, Austrian 1st Army still south of Lublin) and matching Russian-Galicia and Austro-Hungarian-Poland ring keys.

Austro-Hungarian advance into Russian Poland stopped short of Krasnystaw (occupied by X Corps on 30 Aug); 31 Aug front and the A-H ring (new 30 Aug key, revised 2 and 9 Sep) now include Krasnystaw, Zamość and Komarów. Verified the hand-repaired 26/31 Aug East Prussia keys: Gumbinnen/Insterburg (1st Army) and Neidenburg (2nd Army) Russian on 26 Aug, Lemberg Austrian on 31 Aug and Russian on 3 Sep — all now regression claims.

Eastern Front had no position between 22 Jun and 26 Aug or 26 Aug and 31 Oct 1915, so Warsaw (5 Aug), Kovno (17 Aug), Brest-Litovsk (26 Aug) and Vilna (17–19 Sep) never fell on screen and the summer-offensive arrow ended 110 km beyond the front. Added keys 13 May, 3 Jun, 13 Jul, 5 Aug, 19 Aug, 19 Sep (from USMA map 31 lines of 1 May/1 Jun/13 Jul/15 Aug/30 Sep and the dated captures); rerouted the arrow Warsaw–Siedlce–Brest–Kobrin–Pinsk (ends 16 Sep at Pinsk) and added a 'German advance on Kovno and Vilna' arrow.

The 1915 base map paints all of Galicia and Bukovina as Russian for the whole year, so the Gorlice–Tarnów reconquest (Przemyśl 3 Jun, Lemberg 22 Jun) was invisible and Lemberg stayed Russian on the map. New ring 'Central Powers-held Galicia and Bukovina (1915–1916)' = Austro-German side of the front inside Galicia/Bukovina (keys tied to every front key from 1 Jan 1915 to 20 Sep 1916, end 31 Dec 1916), plus a small 'besieged fortress of Przemyśl' ring until its surrender on 22 Mar 1915.

31 Oct 1915 (and 3 Jun 1916, 20 Sep 1916, 5 Sep 1917, 17 Feb 1918) front ran east of Baranovichi and west of Pinsk, i.e. Baranovichi German and Pinsk Russian; the reverse is true (Russians held Baranovichi, Germans took Pinsk on 16 Sep 1915). Front bent west of Baranovichi and east of Pinsk in all these keys. Kovel (abandoned 21 Aug) also sat behind the Russian line on 26 Aug; fixed.

findings.issue: Ober Ost ring overlapped Germany west of Thorn and left a gap along the Suwałki border; rebuilt every key (1914-12-20 to 1918-11-11) from the front plus the clio pre-war Germany–Russia and Austria–Russia borders, traced with a 0.05° outward margin so the app's own-territory clip sets the visible edge. The East Prussian strip around Lyck is included because the 1915 base map wrongly draws it as Russian (it was retaken in Feb 1915).

source.title: USMA West Point Atlas, Map 31: Gorlice–Tarnów breakthrough and Russian withdrawal, 1 May–30 Sep 1915 (Wikimedia Commons)

findings.issue: Eastern Front had no position from 3 Jun to 20 Sep 1916 and the Ober Ost ring interpolated from Oct 1915 straight to Sep 1916, so Lutsk/Volhynia drained away during the winter and the offensive itself never appeared. Added keys 8 Jun (Lutsk, 7 Jun), 20 Jun (Czernowitz 17 Jun, Kolomea 18 Jun, Carpathian foothills), 31 Jul (Stokhod, Brody 28 Jul), 15 Aug (Stanislau 11 Aug), 31 Dec (static), with matching ring keys; the 1916 base map makes Galicia east of 24.3°E and Volhynia Russian all year, which the new Galicia ring and the Ober Ost keys now correct up to the offensive.
Brusilov arrow reached Lutsk only in late August (single 4 Jun–20 Sep span); now 4–9 Jun so Lutsk falls on 7–8 Jun. Added arrow 'Russian Ninth Army takes Czernowitz' (4–20 Jun).

The 1916 base map paints south-east Transylvania (Brașov, Sibiu approaches) as Romania for the whole year, so it showed as neutral before 27 Aug and Allied after Transylvania was retaken (9–16 Oct). New ring 'Central Powers-held Transylvania (1916)' with Romanian Front keys 6 Sep, 15 Sep (revised), 3 Oct (high-water mark near Cristur/Cincu, Sibiu already lost), 9 Oct (Brașov retaken), 19 Oct (back on the frontier).

Romanian Front slid from the 25 Oct frontier straight to the 6 Dec line, and the Falkenhayn arrow crossed the Carpathians at Sibiu in early October. Added 24 Nov key (Jiu valley breakthrough, Craiova 21 Nov, Olt crossed 23 Nov, Danube crossed at Svishtov 23 Nov) with the CP Romania ring; arrow now Vulcan pass–Târgu Jiu–Craiova–Slatina–Pitești–Bucharest, 11 Nov–6 Dec.

source.title: Wikipedia: Second Battle of the Jiu Valley

findings.issue: CP-occupied Romania ring began 15 Sep, so Turtucaia (6 Sep) stayed Romanian; added a 6 Sep key, and a 19 Oct key equal to 15 Sep so the Dobruja ring does not creep north while the Cobadin line held (21 Sep–19 Oct). Romanian invasion arrow retimed to reach Cristur by 29 Sep.

No front position between 17 Feb and 3 Mar 1918 or after 3 Mar, and the chapter had no arrows, so Operation Faustschlag and the occupation of Ukraine were barely visible. Added fronts 24 Feb (Dvinsk 18 Feb, Minsk 21 Feb, Zhitomir 24 Feb, Dorpat/Reval), 15 Mar (Odessa 13 Mar), 10 Apr (Yekaterinoslav 5 Apr, Kharkov 8 Apr), 8 May (Rostov 6 May), matching Ober Ost keys, and four arrows (Dvinsk–Pskov–Narva, Minsk, Kiev, Kharkov–Rostov).

Unoccupied Romania vanishes from the base map after 1916 (Moldavia drawn as Austria-Hungary in 1917–18). New Allied ring 'Unoccupied Romania (Moldavia, with Bessarabia from 1918)' behind the Siret front from 1 Jan 1917, adding Bessarabia after the Romanian entry into Chișinău (26 Jan) and Bender (2 Feb) and the whole province by 8 Mar; ends 7 May 1918 (Treaty of Bucharest). Romanian Front got a 9 Dec 1917 (Focșani armistice) key.

findings.issue: 'Russian-occupied Galicia and Bukovina' had no end, so a Russian (Allied) strip stayed in eastern Galicia to Nov 1918; it now ends on 15 Dec 1917, when Russia leaves the war in the side data.

NOT FIXABLE IN CINEMA DATA: the 1918 base map (clio 1918 German Empire) already contains Belarus, Ukraine to Rostov and the Baltic from 1 Jan 1918, so before the 18 Feb advance Minsk, Kiev and Kharkov show as Central Powers ground and the Ober Ost ring is invisible (own ground). Likewise the 1917 base gives Russian-held Volhynia (Lutsk) to Germany. Needs a base-map/app fix (e.g. use 1917 borders until 3 Mar 1918); occupied areas cannot be drawn as neutral.

NOT FIXED (content.json side data): Romania is an Allied member only for 1916 (to 1916, no toDate), but it stayed at war until the Focșani armistice (9 Dec 1917) and the Treaty of Bucharest (7 May 1918) and re-entered on 10 Nov 1918; after 7 May 1918 the base map paints Moldavia and Bessarabia as Austria-Hungary.

Not drawn: Novogeorgievsk held out behind German lines until 20 Aug 1915, and Przemyśl was besieged inside the Russian ring from Sep 1914 to Mar 1915 (drawn only for 1915, when the base map is Russian; in autumn 1914 the Russian ring still covers the fortress).

great-retreat.text: A German and Austro-Hungarian attack at Gorlice broke the Russian line on 2 May 1915; Przemyśl was retaken on 3 June and Lemberg on 22 June. Over the summer Russia gave up Poland, Lithuania and most of Courland: Warsaw fell on 5 August, Brest-Litovsk on 26 August and Vilna in mid-September, and the front moved hundreds of kilometres east.

brusilov-romania.text: General Brusilov's offensive, launched on 4 June 1916, broke the Austro-Hungarian front and took Lutsk and Czernowitz, Russia's greatest success of the war. Encouraged, Romania joined the Allies in August and invaded Transylvania, but German, Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian armies struck back and took Bucharest on 6 December.
arrows: Falkenhayn breaks through the Carpathians to Bucharest

brest-litovsk.text: After the Bolshevik revolution Russia asked for peace. When talks stalled, German armies advanced almost unopposed in February 1918, and on 3 March Russia signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, giving up Poland, the Baltic lands and Ukraine. German and Austro-Hungarian troops went on to occupy Ukraine, reaching Kharkov in April and Rostov in May.
